entities.name: Amorian dynasty
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Amorian dynasty (Phrygian dynasty), founded 820 CE by Michael II of Amorion (from the Phrygian city of Amorion), ruled the Byzantine Empire for three generations (820-867 CE) through one of its most turbulent periods — the final phase of Byzantine Iconoclasm and its resolution, the emergence of the Bulgarian Khanate as an existential threat, and the missions of Constantine (Cyril) and Methodius that created the Cyrillic alphabet and brought Christianity to the Slavs. Michael III (the 'Drunkard') was assassinated by Basil the Macedonian, ending the dynasty and beginning the greatest Byzantine imperial era.

Michael II (820-829 CE) was a soldier from Amorion who had been imprisoned and was scheduled for execution when he led a coup against Leo V; his guards interrupted the emperor's Christmas morning church service. Michael restored a moderate form of Iconoclasm (the second Iconoclasm phase). His son Theophilos (829-842 CE) was the last Iconoclast emperor — an educated, aesthetically sophisticated ruler who enforced Iconoclasm while admiring Islamic art.

Empress Theodora (widow of Theophilos, regent for Michael III) ended Iconoclasm in 843 CE — the 'Triumph of Orthodoxy,' still celebrated annually in Eastern Orthodox Christianity on the first Sunday of Lent. Michael III (842-867 CE) invited Constantine (Cyril) and Methodius to create an alphabet for the Slavic languages — producing the Glagolitic (later Cyrillic) alphabet — and authorized their mission to Moravia (863 CE) that created Slavic Christian civilization. Basil I assassinated Michael III in 867 CE, founding the Macedonian dynasty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Amorian dynasty — through Empress Theodora's ending of Iconoclasm and Michael III's commissioning of Cyril and Methodius — created two of Byzantine civilization's most durable legacies: the Orthodox Triumph feast still celebrated annually, and the Cyrillic alphabet shaping the written culture of 250 million people.
